newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-PEN PICTURES OF WIMBLEDON WOMEN'S FINALISTS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-PEN PICTURES OF WIMBLEDON WOMEN'S FINALISTS.

text.p: Pen pictures of the women's singles finalists at Wimbledon on Saturday:
MARTINA HINGIS (Switzerland) - WTA ranking 1. Wimbledon seeding 1. Age 16. Height 1.67 m. Weight 52 kg. Grand Slam victories: Australian Open (1997).

Path to the final: Anne Kremer (Luxembourg) 6-4 6-4, Olga Barabanshikova (Belarus) 6-2 6-2, Nicole Arendt (U.S.) 6-1 6-3, Sabine Appelmans (Belgium) 6-1 6-3, Denisa Chladkova (Czech Republic) 6-3 6-2, Anna Kournikova (Russia) 6-3 6-2.

Became the youngest Grand Slam champion in the Open era when she won the Australian Open in January. Took over as world number one from Steffi Graf in March. Despite her low-key approach to the tournament after losing the French Open final to Iva Majoli, she has looked at home on the faster grass surface. Has not dropped a set in the tournament. Last year became youngest-ever Wimbledon champion when she won the women's doubles with Helena Sukova. She is the youngest women's singles Wimbledon finalist, beating the previous record held by Steffi Graf who reached the 1987 final at age 18. She has lost only one match this year -- to Majoli in the French Open. She prefers to stay at the baseline, relying on her consistent forehand and backhand. Czech-born but moved to Switzerland as a child. Named after Martina Navratilova by mother Melanie who is also her coach.
JANA NOVOTNA (Czech Republic) - WTA ranking 4. Seeding 3. Age 28. Height 1.75 m. Weight 63 kg. Grand Slam victories: None.

Path to final: Wiltrud Probst (Germany) 6-4 4-6 6-0, Elena Likhovtseva (Russia) 6-1 4-6 6-4, Gala Leon Garcia (Spain) 6-4 6-2, Mary Joe Fernandez (U.S.) 5-7 6-4 7-5, Yayuk Basuki (Indonesia) 6-3 6-3, Arantxa Sanchez Vicario 6-4 6-2.

Runner-up here in 1993, she is assured of moving to number two in the world rankings after reaching the semifinals here. Her game is naturally suited to grass, but she started the tournament slowly and was taken to three sets three times. Recovered from a knee injury and sore arm midway through tournament and is now playing thrilling serve and volley tennis, although had to pull out of women's doubles on Friday to rest a strained thigh muscle. She beat Monica Seles in Madrid Open final in May and reached the rained out final of the warmup tournament in Eastbourne. Has been a sentimental favourite at Wimbledon since she won hearts by sobbing on Duchess of Kent's shoulder after losing final to Steffi Graf when she had been within reach of victory.
